title: CVE-2026-108142: Critical Veeam Backup & Replication Authorization Bypass
content_md: Veeam has released security updates to address CVE-2026-108142, a critical authorization bypass vulnerability affecting Veeam Backup & Replication 13. The flaw allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass authorization controls associated with the Veeam CDP Coordinator Service. The vulnerability carries a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.1 and affects both Windows-based Veeam Backup & Replication deployments and the Veeam Software Appliance. Veeam disclosed the issue on October 27, 2026 as part of security advisory KB4948. Backup infrastructure is an especially sensitive security target because it contains recovery data and often has privileged connectivity to production systems. An authorization weakness affecting a central backup component therefore warrants immediate attention even though the vendor has not publicly documented the complete exploitation chain. Veeam’s CVSS vector identifies network-based exploitation with low attack complexity, no privileges required, and no user interaction. However, the vector also specifies that additional attack requirements must be present. Veeam has not publicly explained those prerequisites. The vulnerability affects Veeam Backup & Replication 13.1.1.18 and all earlier builds in the 13.1 branch, as well as version 13.0.2.29 and all earlier 13.0 builds.
